chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you pray (Salat) upon the enemy of Allah, say: 'O Allah, we do not know of So-and-so except that he is an enemy of Yours and of Your Messenger. O Allah, fill his grave with fire, and fill his interior with fire, and hasten him to the Fire, for he used to befriend Your enemies and be inimical to Your friends, and hate the People of the House of Your Prophet. O Allah, straiten his grave upon him.'
So when he is raised (from the grave), say: 'O Allah, do not raise his status, and do not purify him.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ نَبِيِّكَ: The People of the House of Your Prophet (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.صَلَّيْتَ: You prayed (referring to Salat al-Janazah or general prayer upon the deceased)
key_terms.فُلَاناً: So-and-so (a placeholder for the name of the deceased)
key_terms.لَا تُزَكِّهِ: Do not purify him (forgive his sins)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific dua to recite when praying over an enemy of Allah in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies the ruling of Salat upon the deceased for those who are not necessarily disbelievers in the technical sense but are 'Nasibi' (rivals of the Ahl al-Bayt), distinguishing their status from general believers. It emphasizes that the supplicant should not affirm their piety (Tazkiyah) nor deny their death, but rather invoke specific divine retribution for their enmity towards the Prophet's household. This practice reflects the theological principle of Walayah (divine friendship) and Barayah (divine enmity) as criteria for spiritual standing.
